kaps_punt: 'n habitat is die plek waar 'n plant of dier lewe; daar is verskillende tipes van habitatte, soos grasveld, bos, rivier, see

items.bewering: 'n Habitat is die plek waar 'n plant of 'n dier lewe.
items.bron: IPBES glossary ('the place or type of site where an organism or population naturally occurs', ipbes.net/glossary-tag/habitat); Collins via dictionary.com/browse/habitat ('the environment in which an animal or plant normally lives or grows').

items.bewering: Gras lewe in die oop veld, en die springbok lewe op dieselfde plek.
items.bron: Springbok in open, level country with few large plants (University of Pretoria habitat study, repository.up.ac.za/handle/2263/85475); range includes Highveld grassland, Karoo and Kalahari, and it avoids dense woodland (animals.worldatlas.com/animals/springbok.html).

items.bewering: Daar is baie soorte habitatte, en hulle is nie eenders nie. Party plekke is oop en vol gras, en ander is vol bome. Sommige habitatte is op die land, en ander is in die water.
items.bron: SANBI grassland biome extract (Low & Rebelo 1996, pza.sanbi.org/node/11259) for open grassland; SANBI on samango monkeys and indigenous forest (sanbi.org/animal-of-the-week/samango-monkey/) for treed habitats; Wikipedia 'River' for freshwater habitats. These are general statements, and each kind is borne out by the later blocks.

items.bewering: 'n Grasveld is 'n oop habitat vol gras met baie min bome.
items.bron: SANBI-hosted extract from Low & Rebelo 1996, Grassland Biome: 'dominated by a single layer of grasses', 'trees are absent, except in a few localized habitats' (pza.sanbi.org/node/11259). 'Baie min bome' is the safe wording.

items.bewering: Die springbok en die meerkat lewe in die droër dele van die grasveld, waar die gras kort is.
items.bron: Meerkat: SANBI, more widespread in the Free State and Northern Cape (sanbi.org/animal-of-the-week/meerkat/); arid, open country with short grass and little woody growth, absent from forest and true desert (Animal Diversity Web, animaldiversity.org/accounts/Suricata_suricatta/). Springbok: dry, open, level country, including Highveld grassland (UP habitat study, repository.up.ac.za/handle/2263/85475). Tested as a set: both animals fit open, dry, short-grass country, and 'droër dele' keeps the claim from saying all grassland. Neither animal is presented as living only there, so there is no false contrast.

items.bewering: 'n Bos is vol hoë bome, en die skaduwee hou dit koel en donker.
items.bron: Studies of forest microclimate: canopy shade lowers summer maximum temperatures inside forests and darkens the forest floor (De Frenne et al. 2013, PNAS; CORDIS FORMICA project, cordis.europa.eu/article/id/444141). SANBI describes South African indigenous forest as high-canopy (samango page). The cause the lesson gives, shade making it cool and dark, is the one the sources give. In this block 'bos' is used for forest, which the sentence itself defines.

items.bewering: Die aap, die luiperd en baie voëls lewe in hierdie koel plek.
items.bron: Samango monkey is South Africa's only guenon that lives only in forest, in high-canopy indigenous forest (SANBI, sanbi.org/animal-of-the-week/samango-monkey/; SANBI Red List, speciesstatus.sanbi.org/assessment/last-assessment/1897/). Leopard: SANBI Red List says densely wooded and rocky areas are its preferred habitat (speciesstatus.sanbi.org/taxa/detail/2172/). Tested as a set: the leopard also lives in grassland, mountains and scrub (same SANBI source). The sentence does not say it lives only in forest, so this is true but incomplete, and incomplete is acceptable.

items.bewering: 'n Rivier is 'n habitat van varswater wat oor klippe en sand loop.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'River': 'a natural stream of fresh water that flows ... towards another body of water'. The article also describes rivers eroding their beds, with rocks sinking to the bottom and finer sand or silt carried further. 'Klippe en sand' describes a typical bed. It does not claim every bed is like that.

items.bewering: Die seekoei en die padda lewe in die water, en riete groei aan die kante.
items.bron: Hippo: SANBI Red List calls it 'an amphibious creature, spending the majority of its day in water, and emerging at night to feed on dry land' (speciesstatus.sanbi.org/taxa/detail/2064/); PBS Nature says the same (pbs.org/wnet/nature/group/mammals/hippopotamus-mammals); grazing about 3 km from water (ultimateungulate.com). Frog: river frogs (Amietia) live in shallow water edged by dense grass (earthpedia.earth.com, Amietia angolensis); adult frogs are generally land-living or semi-aquatic. Several South African rain frogs (Breviceps) never enter water and drown in it (Wikipedia, Breviceps gibbosus and B. rosei). 'Die padda' here is generic, like 'die springbok' and 'die aap' elsewhere in the lesson, so it reads as 'frogs live in the water'. The reeds half is true (see the riete item).
items.regstelling: The habitat claim is right: the river is the habitat of both animals. What is wrong is 'in die water'. The hippo spends its day in the water but comes out at night to eat grass on land, and adult frogs live in and beside water, not only in it. A learner who reasons from the sentence will conclude that a hippo lives and feeds in the water like a fish. Narrow the place rather than cut the animals: they live in and next to the water of the river, or simply in the river habitat. The reeds clause can stay as it is.

items.bewering: Die see is baie groot, en sy water is sout, nie vars nie.
items.bron: The ocean covers about 71% of Earth's surface (Smithsonian Ocean, ocean.si.edu/planet-ocean/seafloor/just-how-big-ocean; NOAA Ocean Today, 'more than 70 percent'). Average salinity is about 35 g/kg (3.5%), and fresh water is defined as far below that (chemeurope.com Sea_water encyclopedia entry; openwaterpedia.com/wiki/Saltwater).

items.bewering: Robbe en visse soos haaie lewe in die see.
items.bron: Sharks are cartilaginous fish, class Chondrichthyes, subclass Elasmobranchii (New World Encyclopedia, 'Cartilaginous fish'; encyclopedia.com 'cartilaginous fishes'). Cape fur seals feed at sea on foraging trips tracked for up to eight months (IRD BENEFIT tracking report; Inter-Research MEPS v649 p201-218). They rest and breed on shore. Checked against the hippo item on purpose: a seal finds all its food in the sea, so 'lewe in die see' does not mislead about where it eats. A hippo's food is on land. No change is needed here, and a writer changing the river sentence need not mirror it here.

items.bewering: habitat: Die plek waar 'n plant of 'n dier lewe.
items.bron: Read on its own, outside its block: IPBES glossary and Collins (as for the first item). The entry is complete and true without the study text.

items.bewering: riete: Lang, dun plante wat in nat grond langs water groei.
items.bron: Common reed, Phragmites australis: SANBI PlantZAfrica (pza.sanbi.org/node/11521), up to 4 m tall, along rivers, streams, dams, vleis and marshes where the ground stays wet; also in shallow standing water (africanlegacy.org.za; fernkloof.org.za). Read on its own, the entry is true. Leaving out shallow standing water makes it incomplete, not false.

opsomming: Een bewering moet reggestel word: 'Die seekoei en die padda lewe in die water' verkeerd. SANBI beskryf die seekoei as amfibies: hy bly bedags in die water en wei snags op droë grond. Volwasse paddas lewe in en langs die water, en party Suid-Afrikaanse paddas gaan nooit in water nie. Vernou die plek ('in en langs die water' of 'in die rivier') en hou albei diere. Al die ander bewerings is met bronne bevestig, ook elke habitat en sy diere as stel getoets en albei begrip-inskrywings op hul eie gelees. Die les bevat geen oortreffende trap en geen vergelyking nie.
